description: We are a team of two Software Engineering students at Concordia University, passionate about technology, problem-solving, and building innovative software solutions. We combine our programming skills and passion for space exploration to explore NASA data and create an interactive, user-friendly application that makes complex scientific information more accessible and useful.
summary:
**Flame in Freefall** is an interactive, SI-powered research dashboard that translates complex NASA Physical Sciences Informatics (PSI) microgravity combustion data into actionable fire safety insights for future Moon and Mars missions.

Built on a normalized Supabase repository, the platform centers on 274 flight test runs from **FLEX (PSI-69)** and **FLEX-2 (PSI-68)** alongside solid and gaseous benchmarks (BASS, Saffire, CFI-G). Users can filter investigations by safety pillar, compare extinction limits side-by-side, and simulate high-oxygen exploration habitats (such as 8.2 psia, ≥30% O₂ lunar bases). A built-in Gemini AI synthesis engine instantly interprets pressure and oxygen boundaries, highlighting where terrestrial fire codes fail and guiding safer spacecraft and habitat design.
details:
Flame in Freefall is an interactive, SI-powered research dashboard that translates complex NASA Physical Sciences Informatics (PSI) microgravity combustion telemetry into actionable fire safety insights.

  • How it works: Built on a normalized Supabase repository and powered by a Gemini AI cross-synthesis engine, it compares core NASA investigations—focusing deeply on 274 flight test runs from FLEX (PSI-69) and FLEX-2 (PSI-68) alongside BASS, Saffire, and CFI-G—to simulate high-oxygen exploration habitats (e.g., 8.2 psia, ≥30% O₂).
  • Benefits & Impact: It simplifies massive datasets into side-by-side extinction matrices and proactive engineering alerts, highlighting where terrestrial fire codes fall short to help design safer spacecraft and lunar/Martian habitats.
  • Tech & Creativity: Combines responsive web design, Supabase, Gemini AI, and NASA PSI data into a scenario-driven safety tool tailored for aerospace engineers and researchers, factoring in real mission atmospheric trade-offs and flight hardware constraints (CIR/MDCA).
